subject.title: fix(message): ignore populated Telegram location on model sends

question: Should trusted agent-runtime Gateway identity be the sole authority that enables Telegram to discard an incidental populated location from a content send, while every ordinary direct/API request remains strictly rejected?
rationale: This is an intentional compatibility and trust-boundary distinction rather than a mechanical correctness question; source evidence supports the intended split, but maintainer intent must confirm the public caller cannot select the trusted path.

options.title: Confirm the private-origin boundary
options.body: Accept the model-tool-only repair after confirming ordinary Gateway clients cannot set the agent-runtime identity used to select it.

options.title: Narrow the authority further
options.body: Require a more explicit internal capability or call-path marker before allowing the normalization.

options.title: Keep strict rejection everywhere
options.body: Reject mixed populated-location payloads for model sends as well, preserving one uniform validation contract.

recommendation.title: Confirm the private-origin boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the model-tool-only repair after confirming ordinary Gateway clients cannot set the agent-runtime identity used to select it.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied discussion explicitly requests this owner confirmation, and no stronger source-history owner is available in the review context.
